bearings.paper_claim: Main model should be log S_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + beta g_(i,t-1) with sector effects and full year effects, raw percent growth and log dollars; dynamic and other terms only as sensitivities.
bearings.paper_location: Boxed formula and design step 4; sections 1, 3 and 13
bearings.system_side: Core tests use lagged raw growth (growth_previous_year_pct) on dollar-level outcomes with national controls pres_year, midterm_year, exp_dem_house, exp_dem_senate and no year effects. Year-FE, log and log-FE forms exist only as ROBUSTNESS variants R-yearFE, R-log, R-logFE. The L3-LV sign flip (+0.352 to -0.477 with sector+year FE; log-FE -0.006) is recorded in the brain note of 2026-09-26, not in code.
bearings.code_ref: sgs_registry.R:33-34 (SGS_GROWTH, SGS_C_CONTROLS); sgs_registry.R:636-682 (R-yearFE, R-log, R-logFE, LOSO, LOYO robustness family); sgs_config.R:79-82
bearings.transfer_conditions: Same study and panel. The review predates the 2026-09-25 rulings; promoting the year-FE log model to primary is Paul's decision, as the review itself says.
bearings.verifier_note: Text confirmed (boxed formula, design step 4, section 13 sensitivities). Registry confirms dollar-level primary with national controls and year-FE and log only as robustness. Flip numbers are from the brain note, not re-derived from output; the L3-LV window is disputed in summary_issues.

bearings.paper_claim: A contraction indicator estimates a level jump at zero, not an asymmetric slope; define contraction on raw growth below zero and use g+ = max(g,0) and g- = max(-g,0) with separate coefficients.
bearings.system_side: The ASYM family splits growth into _pos = max(g,0) and _neg = min(g,0) with a bootstrap equality test. CONTRACT-a and CONTRACT-b keep contracted_prior = 1(g<0) and the registry labels it a level shift. Contraction is defined on raw growth_previous_year_pct. Built _neg is non-positive, so the distress hypothesis predicts a negative slope, the opposite sign to the review's g- coefficient.
bearings.code_ref: sgs_registry.R:311-316 (family header); sgs_registry.R:381-416 (CONTRACT-a, CONTRACT-b, ASYM-SLOPES); sgs_panel.R:1007-1015 (_pos and _neg construction)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct. The sign must be flipped when comparing the built _neg slope with the review's g- coefficient. Both ASYM and CONTRACT are EXTENSION labels, not primary.
bearings.verifier_note: Verdict risk 3 and section 14 bullets 2-3 match the code, including the sign convention and the level-shift labelling of the indicator.

bearings.paper_claim: f(P-M)+gM equals fP+(g-f)M, so Shift adds no information beyond P and current control M; a test of current versus expected power needs both terms in the model.
bearings.system_side: exp_shift = exp_dem minus cur_dem is built per chamber (sgs_panel.R:230-235). The contribution core controls carry exp_dem but not cur_dem, so H4shift-C enters exp_shift alone and cannot separate P from M in that model. For lobbying the code notes that cur_dem is retained and the shift terms reparametrise the core model. SHIFT preview over 2021-25, chamber-stacked: -0.04, p 0.76 (brain note, run analysis-R-20260926T070630Z).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds whenever a year-level probability enters with or without current control; within-chamber year effects would absorb both terms anyway. H4shift is labelled EXPLORATORY in code.
bearings.verifier_note: The algebra and the lobbying reparametrisation note are confirmed. The original phrase restricted contrast was an inference, not a code note; reworded here to say the contribution model cannot separate P from M without cur_dem.

bearings.paper_claim: The main campaign outcome should be corporate and trade-association PAC disbursements to congressional candidates, with individual, party, super PAC and independent-expenditure channels separate; never combine donor-to-PAC receipts with PAC-to-candidate payments.
bearings.system_side: Ruling R4 sets contributions = Mentat general giving across all recipient categories (DV label general giving (04), all recipient categories). The 2026-09-26 ruling keeps non_giving other-receipt rows, for example Stripe 464K to NRSC in 2021-22, in every test. Workbook 08 (README window 2019-2026, 2019-2020 missing): 5.6 percent of general-giving dollars reach House or Senate candidate committees. Company-PAC gifts are 8.84 percent of 2021-25 nominal giving, per the overlap check.
bearings.code_ref: sgs_config.R:79; sector_growth_study README lines 83 and 87 (data 04 and 08 notes); brain topic note lines 96, 127, 194
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paul's rulings govern scope. The review's point bears on how C1-C3 are read as a capacity mechanism and on the mixed receipt types, not on whether the series is collected.
bearings.verifier_note: Ruling text and DV label confirmed in config and notes. The contradiction stands; the non_giving receipts are the case the never-combine rule addresses most directly.

bearings.paper_claim: With five to ten sectors, report small-sample cluster corrections, restricted wild-cluster inference, cluster leverage and leave-one-sector-out checks; bootstrap p-values are not a guarantee; Driscoll-Kraay only as sensitivity with about 18 years.
bearings.system_side: Every focal term uses a wild cluster restricted bootstrap-t with Webb six-point weights, clusters = sectors. sgs_descriptive_note marks a term descriptive when p below 2/6^G cannot be reached with G sectors. LOSO and LOYO variants are built. No Driscoll-Kraay estimator appears in sgs_estimate.R (grep returned no match). Cluster leverage was not located in the lines read.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct. The review's point that no method repairs few independent units applies to every pooled growth coefficient.
bearings.verifier_note: Header, descriptive note and LOSO and LOYO confirmed. Driscoll-Kraay absence confirmed by grep. The brief's D-K request is in the brain note of 2026-09-25 (line 271).

bearings.paper_claim: Some 538 models use fundraising, so explaining contributions with them creates a feedback problem; prefer polls-only. More monthly rows improve timing resolution, not the number of independent elections (about 9 elections, 6 flips): exploratory.
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W uses 538 Lite as primary. The code says Lite is not polls-only (it imputes unpolled races) but omits the Classic and Deluxe fundraising fundamentals. Rows are gated on available_at. Reported estimate, House 2022, 17 weeks, Lite: -3.47 pp D share per expected D seat, block-bootstrap p 0.0086 (3-week) and 0.0174 (5-week); the Holm-adjusted values 0.034 and 0.070 are in the brain note. Labelled one election and EXPLORATORY in code notes.
bearings.code_ref: sgs_seats.R:18-22 (header); sgs_seats.R:86-96 (Lite labelling and primary rationale); sgs_seats.R:763-771 (538 Lite availability gating)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds until 2018 and 2020 weekly money joins; even then each further cycle adds one independent election, per the code notes.
bearings.verifier_note: Code labelling and gating confirmed. The -3.47 estimate and p-values come from the brain run record, not re-derived. Section 5 and section 7 text confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: Value added, gross output, profits and assets are different quantities; output growth is not spare cash; corporate PAC budgets come from voluntary SSF contributions, so a capacity mechanism fits lobbying more than PAC giving.
bearings.paper_location: Overall verdict risk 1; sections 2 and 10; BEA definitions paragraph
bearings.system_side: The cycle model's 50/50 budget term uses IBISWorld REAL annual revenue growth with a one-year lag (_ibis_path). D-116 (2026-10-08) sets x = 0 for company PACs and documents the drop; the term remains for other measures. The sector-study backtest (last-year naive MAE 3.63 vs +growth 3.99, LobbyView targets 2014-2023, brain note) tests the study growth term, not the IBIS budget rule.
bearings.code_ref: giving_forecast.py:1389-1401 (D-116 and cycle-model documentation); giving_forecast.py:1490-1493 (_ibis_path); giving_forecast.py:1881-1884 (x = 0 for company PACs)
bearings.transfer_conditions: The backtest does not isolate any revenue-to-spending link, so it cannot be cited as evidence that the IBIS budget rule is weak. Use only as a fact about the growth term's forecast error in that window.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claims and the D-116 and IBIS lag details are confirmed. The original transfer condition read the backtest as showing a weak revenue-to-spending link; that does not follow because the backtest tests a different term over 2014-2023 targets.

bearings.paper_claim: LDA in-house expenses include retained-firm payments and lobbying-related association dues, so adding client expenses, firm revenues and association expenses double-counts; keep the series separate or deduplicate.
bearings.system_side: The Mentat notice states that PAC, candidate-share and lobbying amounts are separate accounts and that the two lobbying series are never summed (giving_forecast.py:2074). The sector study keeps lobby_income (outside-firm) and lobby_expenses (self-filer) as separate DVs (sgs_config.R:80-81). Trade-association overlap is not handled separately in the config read. The side-by-side display claim comes from a Melange commit message and was not read in code.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct for any sector total. Trade-association overlap is not yet handled separately, per the bearing; not confirmed by code read here.
bearings.verifier_note: Never-summed notice and separate DVs confirmed. The display claim and association-overlap status were not confirmed in code and are not needed for the verdict.

related.why: Imai and Kim (Political Analysis 2021) caution what two-way fixed effects identify for causal claims; the review makes sector and year FE its primary design, so the caution applies.
Title reports surprisingly low overlap between organizational lobbying and campaign expenditures, which supports modelling PAC giving and lobbying separately. The review does not cite it.
Title covers corporate lobbying, PACs and market concentration; the review asks for concentration and active-actor counts, so the topical link holds.
Paper text reports lobbying patterns synchronized with electoral cycles, which is the phase pattern full year effects absorb. The review does not cite it; the link is topical.
Paul's client report on LD-2 lobbying disclosure is plausibly built on the same LDA filings. The review does not mention it and no data-level match was checked.

summary_issues: The L3-LV window 2008-2023 is not supported. The code's LobbyView primary window rule is 2020-2025 with a fallback (sgs_registry.R:27), and the only window in the notes is the 2014-2023 backtest. Treat the window as unverified and likely wrong.
The UNSTRATIFIED label for the L3-LV slope was not checked against any run output; the labelling function exists (sgs_estimate.R:250-257) but no printed result was read.

The phrase the later Codex audit vindicated the review's main warning overstates the record. The brain note shows the sign flip and that growth adds nothing to fit (adj R2 0.884717 vs 0.884690), on 5 sectors. Say consistent with the warning instead.

The claim that the note reads as an external AI reviewer's output filed under Paul's name is unsupported speculation. The text is first person, the metadata names Paul, and Paul's own project notes call it the 09-24 review (memory sector-growth-study-lane-2026-09-25, line 90). Remove it.

Paul's recorded position as returns literature and deep-pockets reading is not found in the brain note. The brain note supports only his seems to confirm reading for lobbying and champions (brain line 230), and the summary should keep only that.
The Huneeus link was dropped: the review does not cite Huneeus or any deep-pockets motivation (zero matches in the text), so the related rationale was false.
